summary: MiroTalk SFU is a self-hosted web application designed to facilitate real-time video conferences across multiple browsers and platforms. It utilises selective forwarding units to handle media streams, aiming to support high-resolution video outputs up to 4k. The project is distributed under an open-source licence and containerised for deployment.
goodFor: It suits teams or individuals looking for a dedicated, self-hosted video conferencing node that they can run entirely on their own infrastructure.
watchOut: The AGPL-3.0 licence carries strict copyleft implications if you modify and distribute the code or offer it as a hosted service. Additionally, managing real-time media routing can impose significant bandwidth and CPU demands on your server.
deployNotes: As a Node.js application packaged with Docker, you will typically need to configure a reverse proxy to handle TLS termination and manage persistent storage or environment variables according to your setup.
